comments.author: Hernan
comments.body: It all depends on the ship being modded. If the required rank for that ship and round (the req goes up for each round) is really high, then success rate suffers compared to lower rank ships. I use this part extensively, and the only time I've got less than calc is when the required rank for the ship is 20 or more, and that's normal. This is why people say certain ships like FIS are tough to mod, you need a lot of luck to get good results.

comments.author: Lewis
comments.body: Just to add: This is also why you should plan your builds to include the most important stats in the early rounds, and/or the use the parts with the worst penalties in the early rounds. The increased success rate of lower ranked rounds will help mitigate those penalties to some degree.

comments.author: Jean
comments.body: One more thing: There is no way to tell which part failed on each round. It's not really rational to blame this part, when any of them could have failed. It could have even been different parts failing each round...

comments.author: Kicker
comments.body:
there is a rumor/myth that using the same part in the same build (ie 2 anti-roll tanks) leads to more fails. I don't know if this is true or not, but just in case of that I do set my builds up to avoid using two of the same parts in the same build. If that means buying a traverse rope to use instead it's just a couple more million to cover the bases.

Paneling always goes on the very last build for the ship unless it's a panel/reset job for the reason given earlier, more likely to get a bad build result on the later improvements.
